title: Capability alignment and tenancy model for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define the RBAC v2 role model and capability alignment across Redwood resource tenancy levels. This ticket produces the canonical resource hierarchy, a capability-to-role binding guide, and a permissions matrix that covers hosted/Dedicated/Private. Output will include migration instructions from RBAC v1, audit logging requirements, SSO/SAML group -> role mapping guidance, and admin safety constraints (break-glass, emergency escalation). The design must be implementable in the existing auth service with minimal runtime latency and support caching and bulk-evaluation paths for high-throughput inference routes.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical resource hierarchy document published and reviewed (Confluence link in artifacts)
Permission matrix mapping roles to capabilities for at least 12 common resources and 8 built-in roles
Design includes inheritance and override semantics, conflict resolution, and policy evaluation order
Migration plan for RBAC v1 -> v2 with scripts and DB changes listed
SSO/SAML mapping pattern documented with example IdP attributes and SCIM provisioning flow
Audit logging schema defined with required events and retention guidance
Security review completed and sign-off from Security and Compliance teams
design_decisions: Resource hierarchy will be tenant-first: global -> organization -> project -> model -> deployment -> route
Capabilities expressed as atomic verbs (read:list, read:get, write:update, admin:manage, deploy:start, audit:view, billing:read) to allow composition into roles
RoleSets: users may be assigned named role sets (team-level roleSets) in addition to tenant-scoped role bindings to simplify cross-project permissions
Explicit deny is supported but discouraged; evaluation order: explicit deny -> explicit allow at same scope -> inherited allow from parent scopes
Service accounts can have non-human roleSets with token-scoped TTLs; impersonation requires separate consented capability 'admin:impersonate'
Break-glass admin is timeboxed, logged to a dedicated immutable audit stream, and requires 2nd factor confirmation via SSO session extension
tradeoffs: Flattened capability verbs increase flexibility but make manual audits harder; to mitigate we provide generated matrices and exportable CSVs
Caching authorizations improves runtime latency but introduces window where recent binding changes aren't immediate; TTL default is 60s with an admin invalidation API
Supporting explicit deny makes principle-of-least-privilege expressive but complicates evaluation and testing; chosen to include explicit deny only for high-risk scopes (billing, admin:impersonate)
Modeling tenancy at fine granularity (per-route) increases precision but multiplies ACL entries; we use inheritance plus sparse overrides to limit row count
implementation_plan: 1) Schema changes: add role_sets, grants, grant_audit tables (see db_schema_changes) - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/1284
2) Authorizer core: implement evaluation order and caching layer - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/342
3) SSO/SAML mapping: add IdP attribute mapping config and SCIM sync - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity/pull/198
4) Console and API: expose roleSet management, preview permission simulator, and admin invalidation endpoint - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/911
5) Migration tool: RBAC v1 export/import with reconciliation reports - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/77
6) Integration tests and load tests, then staged rollout (see rollout_plan)
migration_plan: Export RBAC v1 bindings to canonical CSV and run reconciliation to suggested roleSets
Run dry-run import in staging and compare effective permissions with a policy-simulator
Provide a 'compat' roleSet for any unmatched v1 grant to avoid downtime
Two-week staged rollout: 20% orgs -> 50% -> full, with monitoring on auth error rates and latencies
Backout path: revert to v1 bindings using preserved export if discrepancies detected
db_schema_changes: grants (id, role_set_id, principal_type, principal_id, resource_path, scope, effect, created_by, created_at)
grant_audit (id, grant_id, action, performed_by, performed_at, metadata)
indexed materialized view: effective_grants(tenant_id, principal_id, resource_path, scopes) for fast lookups
audit_logging_integration: Audit events must include actor (user_id), actor_identity (idp, saml_nameid), action, resource_path, scope, decision (allow|deny), evaluation_trace_id, request_id, timestamp, and optional session_fingerprint. Break-glass events must be written to an immutable append-only topic with 7-year retention for compliance. Logs should be wire-compatible with existing observability pipelines and exportable to customer-managed S3 for Private deployments.
sso_saml_mapping: Support attribute-based role assignment: map SAML attribute 'groups' -> roleSet (example mapping exported in artifacts)
SCIM provisioning creates service_account principals and can assign initial roleSets
IdP assertion validation must include audience and message replay protection per SAML profile
Provide an admin UI to override automated mappings and surface 'orphaned' groups for review
performance_considerations: Authorization cache: in-memory LRU per auth node with 60s TTL and global invalidation endpoint
Bulk-eval API: evaluation for up to 200 principals at once to support analytics and Console preview
Add indices on (tenant_id, principal_id, resource_path) and materialized views for effective grants
Estimate: additional 8% p95 auth latency under 1M RPS service; will run a canary with load-driver to validate
rollout_plan: Canary on staging and internal infra for 2 weeks
Stage 1: 10% small orgs (non-critical) for 48 hours, monitor error/latency and permission diffs
Stage 2: 50% orgs with automated rollback window and manual approval
Stage 3: full rollout with customer-facing migration notifications and opt-out compatibility window
Post-rollout: 30-day audit and follow-up migration sweeps for edge cases
review_comments: PM (Lina Gomez): 'Ensure roleSet UX is simple for infra teams; add a preview that shows effective permissions before apply.'
Design (Renee Cho): 'Console needs a bulk assignment flow and CSV templates — I've attached a draft UI spec in artifacts.'

notes: Prototype used in spike showed 40% fewer DB rows with roleSets vs per-principal grants for orgs with 200+ projects
We must coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams to expose retention and audit export controls
Consider future support for ABAC tags on resources; design kept extensible to allow tag predicates
test_plan: Unit tests for evaluation engine including explicit deny scenarios
Integration tests with SSO SAML IdP simulator and SCIM sync
Load tests simulating 100k authorization checks/sec with cache and 1k/sec without cache
Chaos test: simulate cache invalidation storms and ensure fallbacks do not overwhelm DB
